Promotion to main is the worker's own act (leader instruction 2026-11-18): wait for the dev push run on the squash SHA (use the FULL 40-char SHA with gh run list --commit) to be green, open a dev->main PR, let its checks go green on that exact SHA, re-fetch to confirm origin/dev has not moved, then git push origin origin/dev:main bare, then fetch and report origin/main and origin/dev by ref. Batch tracker writes into one promotion where you can.

WHAT LANDED THIS SESSION: #372 (WCLI-21 run-directory execution choice, WCLI-177 closed), #370 (4a-2b-2 part A, squash dd4aef1, after three opus rounds), #389 (follow-up 1, squash f2caf31), #395 (follow-up 2 incl. Mutant bodies must be biome-formatted or the format gate fails before any test runs.

PART B (NOT STARTED, and its P0 wiring is UNBLOCKED once #399 lands; NB1 / DEC-262 (a34) is done): scripts/qualify-linux.ts rebuilt on the landed modules (qualify-linux-shim.ts, -rows.ts, -support.ts), NOT revived from 760d9f8 (take only its structure; git show 760d9f8:scripts/qualify-linux.ts), --build <dir> (buildExecutable already takes a target, so scripts/build.ts needs no change), and the source test that the harness spawns no reboot, shutdown, systemctl, poweroff, halt, init and no sh -c, proven both ways with a mutant. Guard main with import.meta.main so no test can import and run it; the source test reads file text and must not trip on a comment saying never reboot. Phases map to the WCLI-172 plan P0-P4 (facts P0, deliver P1, seal P2, unseal P3, clean P4); the packaged ward flow (pty bridge, ward commands) is 4a-3, NOT B. Per DEC-262 (a32)-(a34) as landed in requiredChecks: P0 runs ONLY id -G, uname -a, tpm2_getcap --version and ls -l /dev/tpmrm0, no interposer, no write anywhere (including ~/ward-t26-wcli21), and owes only effective-groups-recorded, tpm-device-present, tpm2-tools-present; expectedTools has NO facts entry; the shim rows and window row apply at seal and unseal, clean keeps the shim rows; tcti-is-device-tpmrm0 and handle-lists-unchanged are owed by P2, P3, P4; real-ward-metadata-unchanged by P1-P4; python3-recorded by P3 only, and P3 fails closed until part B produces it (the interpreter it ACTUALLY RUNS for /usr/bin/python3 -I, path and version, from that run, not a separate probe). The WCLI-21 notes marked BINDING ON PART B hold the rest: control call stdout read as latin1 and run outside the phase call log; the P2 baseline / P4 comparison / P1 ward-metadata baseline wiring; the production call passes NO third argument to listWindowRoots (it is a test seam); the window listing fails on any non-UTF-8 name whoever owns the directory, so one stray such name under /tmp, /dev/shm or $TMPDIR fails every run, and the remedy is the operator removing or renaming it (Ward never does). Run-directory choice (DEC-262 execution choice, on WCLI-21): P1 deliver creates ~/ward-t26-wcli21 EXCLUSIVELY (one non-recursive mkdir, mode 0700, fails if present) and writes the binaries into it; facts, seal, unseal and clean each re-assert it with lstat (real directory not symlink, owned by the running uid, mode exactly 0700, the ruled literal path; any mismatch stops the phase); each phase makes its own interposers-<phase> exclusively inside it (non-recursive, fails if present, 0700); P4 deletes by the literal path. Advisor points carried from WCLI-177: one window listing per phase, never spanning the reboot (roots: run directory, tmpdir(), /tmp, /dev/shm; needlesFor searches state.json for the KEY forms only, every other file for key plus nonce); runTool throws on non-zero, so catch it and record exitCode in HandleRead; read tools.log with readToolLog (latin1); check on P0 that the jetson's /usr/bin/env supports -0 (else every call logs ENV-SPLIT and the run fails closed); a PR over about 400 lines is flagged and a split proposed before pushing.

EVERY HOLD THAT STANDS: do not merge #399 without an approval naming its head. Part B is held until #399 lands; then build it, one PR per slice, each reviewed (opus) before it lands. --build CLEARANCE (leader, as held): CLEARED for when B reaches it: local Mac, bun scripts/qualify-linux.ts --build <dir>, an expected cache hit on bun-linux-aarch64-v1.3.14 (~/.bun/install/cache/bun-linux-aarch64-v1.3.14, 91801560 bytes, dated Sep 7); run it with whatever verbose or network logging Bun offers, record whether any fetch happened, record the sha256 of the cached runtime and of both output binaries; if it tries to reach anything other than Bun's GitHub release, STOP and REPORT; if the first cross-compile needs a network build host, name it before it runs. PROCESS RULES THAT HOLD: nothing merges before the leader relays an Opus verdict on the exact head; mutant predictions COMMITTED before any run and never edited, observations appended, a driver restoring every mutated file after each mutant (the drivers lived in the previous session scratchpad and are gone: apply a string replacement, run the test files, record the red test names, restore, loop); branch first, never commit on dev; git push alone in its own Bash call (the guard hook refuses a composed push); gh pr merge bare with --match-head-commit from a headRefOid read; merge origin/dev before a quest write; quest edits take --actor ward-cli-worker --actor-kind delegated-agent --accountable-human jdnewhouse; edit files with python or the Edit tool; reply to the leader by native team mail to team-lead; answer each nonce check with exactly its line; fence DEC-182 (1): stop and report before committing a CI workflow, ruleset, dependency or lockfile, settings or permissions, plugin manifest, install or session hook, build, runtime pin, launcher, pins, required-check logic, release or publish path, auth, secrets or credentials change. Skills: opum-handoff (restore), opum-sdlc, quest. bun 1.3.14; quest is on PATH via ~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.22.2/bin when command -v quest fails.

WHAT COST TIME (so the successor skips it): (1) the ownership guard refuses any shell-built redirect target ("> $D/x.log") and any git fetch inside opum-doc; use literal paths or a pipe, and read opum-doc by ref with git -C /Volumes/external/repos/opum-doc show --no-ext-diff --no-textconv origin/dev:.quest/planning.json (the ref is as last fetched, so say so when quoting). (2) The store text of a DEC-262 entry can differ from the relay text; quote from the store byte-exact (a34 differed from the relay in four places). (3) A typed 40-char SHA for --match-head-commit fails with a coercion error; copy it from the headRefOid read. (4) quest task complete needs In Progress first (To Do -> Done is illegal). (5) A merge of origin/dev conflicts on .quest/tasks/WCLI-21.json (every note write is one JSON line): take theirs and re-add the branch's note with quest task edit --add-note, run from the repo directory. (6) Bun readdirSync with encoding buffer returns plain Uint8Arrays, not Buffers. (7) A directory holding a non-UTF-8 name is unlisted as a whole, so a sound file for a window test goes in a second root. (8) Biome: bun run lint is the gate (assist is off); a bare biome check reports organizeImports noise. (9) gh pr close --delete-branch also removes the local branch when it is checked out elsewhere; git branch -D then reports not found, which is fine. (10) ScheduleWakeup/sleep loops are blocked: use gh pr checks --watch, and expect "no checks reported" for the first seconds after a push (run it again).
